title: Box Model
question: Explain the CSS box model.
answer:
Every element is a box with content, padding, border, and margin. width and height by default apply to content box.

box-sizing: border-box includes padding and border in the declared width, simplifying layouts.

Margin collapse occurs between adjacent vertical margins of block elements. Understanding the box model is foundational for spacing bugs.
examples:
* { box-sizing: border-box; }
.card { width: 300px; padding: 16px; border: 1px solid #ccc; }

title: Flexbox
question: How does CSS Flexbox work?
answer:
Flexbox lays out items along a main axis and cross axis. Container properties: display flex, flex-direction, justify-content, align-items, gap.

Item properties: flex-grow, flex-shrink, flex-basis, align-self. Flexbox excels at centering, distributing space, and one-dimensional layouts.

Use flex-wrap for responsive rows. flex: 1 is shorthand for flex-grow 1, flex-shrink 1, flex-basis 0%.
examples: .row { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; gap: 1rem; }

title: CSS Grid
question: When would you use CSS Grid over Flexbox?
answer:
Grid handles two-dimensional layouts: rows and columns simultaneously. Flexbox handles one-dimensional distribution.

Grid features: grid-template-columns/rows, fr units, grid-area, implicit vs explicit tracks, and subgrid.

Common pattern: Grid for page layout, Flexbox for component internals. They compose well together.

title: Specificity
question: How is CSS specificity calculated?
answer:
Specificity ranks selectors: inline styles beat IDs beat classes/attributes/pseudo-classes beat elements. !important overrides normal cascade except against equal !important.

Order matters when specificity is equal—the last rule wins. Avoid escalating specificity wars; prefer single-class selectors and CSS variables.

:where() reduces specificity of its arguments. Understanding specificity fixes "why won't my style apply" bugs.

title: BEM
question: What is the BEM naming convention?
answer:
BEM stands for Block Element Modifier. Block is standalone (menu). Element is part of a block (menu__item). Modifier is a variant (menu__item--active).

It reduces specificity conflicts and clarifies component structure. Pairs well with component-based frameworks.

Alternatives include CSS Modules and utility-first Tailwind. Consistency matters more than the exact methodology.

title: CSS Variables
question: How do CSS custom properties (variables) work?
answer:
Define with --name: value on a selector (often :root). Use with var(--name, fallback).

Unlike preprocessor variables, custom properties are live in the cascade and can change with media queries or JavaScript.

Ideal for theming: dark mode toggles update variables on html or body. They inherit and scope naturally.

title: Responsive Design
question: What are best practices for responsive CSS?
answer:
Mobile-first media queries use min-width breakpoints. Use relative units (rem, %, vw) for scalability.

Fluid typography with clamp(), flexible grids, and responsive images improve all viewports. Touch targets should be at least 44px.

Test real devices. Container queries (@container) style components based on parent size, not just viewport.

title: Z-Index Stacking
question: How does the CSS stacking context work?
answer:
z-index only compares elements within the same stacking context. New contexts are created by positioned elements with z-index, opacity < 1, transform, filter, and more.

A high z-index inside a low context cannot escape above siblings outside it. This causes modal and dropdown bugs.

Fix by moving overlays to a top-level portal or ensuring the parent creates the intended context.
examples:
.modal-backdrop { position: fixed; z-index: 1000; }
.dropdown { position: absolute; z-index: 10; }
